name: John Oldmixon
credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: John Oldmixon (1673–1742) was an English Whig historian and pamphleteer, author of a critical history of England and a target of Pope's Dunciad. He also wrote songs and light verse.

The poem here is the one printed under his name in Frederick Locker's Lyra Elegantiarum (London: E. Moxon, 1867), an anthology of vers de société and vers d'occasion by deceased authors; the texts follow that first edition.

poems.title: I lately vow'd, but 'twas in haste
poems.author: John Oldmixon
poems.collection: Lyra Elegantiarum, ed. Frederick Locker (London: E. Moxon, 1867)
poems.text:
I lately vow'd, but 'twas in haste.
That I no more would court
The joys that seem when they are past
As dull as they are short.

I oft to hate my mistress swear,
But soon my weakness find;
I make my oaths when she's severe.
But break them when she's kind.
